_: One run of any command. The same shape for fix, ship, sprint and mvp — what differs is which fields are filled. Written by the run, read by the run that resumes it, by the reviewer, and by whatever launched it. JSON because a script reads it; the owner reads the pull request instead.
_step: queued | design | build | verify | deliver | done | blocked | skipped. The last three are terminal: a driver stops watching a run that reaches one, so nothing may leave it there while still working.
_parent: The run this one continues from, when a batch chains its features. Its run file carries the decisions this one inherits; its branch is this one's base.
_deliver: pr — open one at the end, the default. branch — push and stop, because a batch delivers its features together.
approach: one sentence: how this is being built here
seams: the points the tests sit at
_unmet: Tests this run left marked `agent-kit:unmet` — a promise of the entry the product does not keep. One line each: the entry, what the code does instead, and what it waits for. The closing session reads only run files, so a mark left out of here does not reach the batch's pull request.
_deferred: Work this run decided not to do, one line each — the same lines it wrote into docs/technical_debt.md. Delivering a pull request itself, the run has already written them there; inside a batch, the closing session carries them over.
_closed_debt: Items of docs/technical_debt.md this run finished and deleted from the file, one line each. The ledger only shrinks in a commit that does the work, and this is where a batch's report gets the count from.
_window: The tmux session the owner briefed this run in, so a driver knows where to put its news. Only a batch has one, and a batch without one simply runs unnarrated.
